title: Building Exclusively with Fable vs fable for orchestration and other models for implementation? Does anyone notice a difference in quality of outputs?
author: zmizzy
selftext:
Like most claude users I primarily have fable do the orchestration/planning while the other models do the implementation (primarily opus medium). But i have this fable reset to use and thought i would spend a week's usage using only fable for every task for a few features. From planning to implementation, with main sessions and subagents I'll have fable do everything. 

Has anyone here experimented with these two strategies enough to speak about the differences in output quality? I know fable is probably a little better in building assets, which I'm interested in hearing about, but ill be focusing my building efforts mostly on gameplay mechanics, systems and features.

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body:
opus is good enough for most programming tasks, but fable is noticably better at driving blender

i feel that you'll just need to try it in your domain a couple times and see what you think

replies.author: zmizzy
replies.body: i wasnt aware of that. im just now realizing that my asset creation skill has probably been using opus this whole time. I might have to spend a chunk of the usage just having fable make some pretty assets​

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body: be warned, fable blender hungers for tokens

replies.author: zmizzy
replies.body: good to know. with the fable resets I'm willing to burn some extra for better outputs so it will make for a good test.

replies.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
replies.body:
I'd like to hear other people's opinions about this too, but I've started using Mixar. It's basically a port of blender that's designed more towards making itself easier for an AI to use (this is my understanding from what I've seen). And I consistently get better results from it than blender by itself, in a shorter period. It does require its own monthly subscription though, which you have to be able to justify to yourself. I haven't tried to have fable control either though, just opus through fable as the coordinator. 

I also have a fable reset waiting, so I guess I'll try to have fable run the modeling process itself too and see if I'm happier with the results.

replies.author: StoneCypher
replies.body: i've never even heard of this.  thank you for the tip; i'll look into it.

replies.author: Putrid_Clue_2127
replies.body:
I found it on someone's YouTube channel, it was the first I'd heard of it too. This past week I did some tests with opus in blender and opus in mixar, and the models I was getting from mixar were actually consistently better, faster. I have a lottt of testing left to do though. Apparently there are a few things that Claude is still using the blender runner for though. It created a table for me for what is done in both apps

Edit: I did have to tell Claude to look up mixar and read the documentation of how to use it. Because at first it assumed it couldn't do most things in it until the actual documentation told it what it could be used for.

replies.author: MidSerpent
replies.body: I use ChatGPT for blender because it’s image generation is the best around and can decompose concept art into easy to model turn arounds and pieces.

comments.author: MidSerpent
comments.body:
Burn rate is definitely lower with Fable as an orchestrator.

In my experience you rarely need the Fable level of thinking in sub agents because they’re working on briefs written by a fable dispatcher, but that also depends on your orchestration workflow.

comments.author: HardSellStudios
comments.body: I found that overall Fable is pretty good at picking up some oversights and the best use case I found for fable so far has been reviewing things from Opus and that seems to be the best bang for the buck that I found so far . While it is definitely very capable what I've noticed is that nine times out of 10 it will fire up Opus agents to do work so I've started using it primarily for managing the instances that I have started up manually.

comments.author: tworc2
comments.body: Fable for planning and overall review. You don't even need them as an orchestrator. Have a good plan, milestones, when another instance should be called and so on. Even a dumb model can work as orchestrator provided you made the right pipeline and guardrails
